article.title: Estimate what a send will cost
article.excerpt: Segments × destinations × sender type is the whole formula. Here is how to work it out before the invoice arrives.

p: You are not billed by characters but by segments, and a message that exceeds one segment is split — each part carries a small header, which reduces how much text fits in the parts after the first.
sections.note: One emoji is enough to move an otherwise Latin message into UCS-2, which more than halves the characters per segment. That single character can double the cost of a send.

sections.h: Multiply by destination and sender type
p: Cost is per segment per destination, at the rate your own provider charges you. Nothing is repriced on the way through, so the rate that applies is the one on your contract — which is exactly why estimating cost is a matter of reading your provider’s price list with the segment count in hand.
list: A long code is usually cheaper per message but more heavily rate-limited than a short code.
Some destinations bill differently for an alphanumeric sender ID.
Concatenated segments are billed individually, not as one message.

p: Usage is derived from the same message log the console shows, so a filtered log and a usage figure cannot disagree. After a real send, filter the log to the window and count the rows — that is the number your provider will bill.
